prompt: Practice Question for IELTS Submit your responses and I will evaluate each response. An increasing number of people are choosing to have cosmetic surgery in order to improve their appearance. Why are more people choosing to have operation to change the way they look? Do you think this a positive or negative development?Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
Regarding the question of why the number of cosmetic surgeries has increased, I am of the opinion that social pressures continue to increase due to the overexposure to social media. This strikes me as an increasingly dangerous trend, because it preys on vulnerabilities.

With the widespread access to social media, our society has become increasingly reliant on being perceived as conventionally attractive. Content creators measure their success in money and engagement through comments and „likes".

Therefore, to be successful, one has to steadily attract new followers and keep them motivated to comment on your content. YouTube's statistics show the continued success of „beauty-influencers" throughout the years. While other trends typically experience fluctuations in popularity, the interest in being seen as beautiful has not diminished. This leads to a culture in which being beautiful is a legitimate profession.  This continued stream of revenue is only feasible, however, if the beauty of the creator is upheld. Because of this, surgeries have become the standard to ensure long-lasting youth and good looks. The film industry has faced similar issues for decades, with stars being both praised and criticised for their choices regarding cosmetic procedures. Consequently, these trends can lead to many fans emulating the behaviours of their idols.

Since cosmetic surgeries have become so commonplace online, many young women especially feel the need to fit into this skewed perception of beauty. This has been an issue in my youth over a decade ago, but when asked, younger acquaintances have assured me that the pressures have increased drastically. Feelings and fears commonly described, such as fear-of-missing-out or „FOMO“, along with the social pressure to present a filtered, perfect version of oneself online, may result in an increase in cosmetic procedures.

There is a myriad of dangers associated with this development, from an increase in rates of body dysmorphia to the financial strain, especially on young people. It is not uncommon for teenagers to feel uncomfortable in their changing bodies. But rigid, unachievable standards set by beauty gurus online only heighten the discrepancy between a young person's appearance and their idolised aesthetic. The prevalence of surgical means to rectify perceived flaws is presented as the correct, socially acceptable choice. This can have detrimental effects on teenagers, encouraging dangerous behaviours such as self-harm tendencies and other maladaptive coping mechanisms. When the possibility of having a surgical procedure performed is offered, those desperate enough are willing to go into debt to afford it. Especially in countries like the United States, this debt can accompany somebody for decades to come. It might even impede other choices, such as going to college or buying a house, due to negative credit scores.

Overall, the rise in cosmetic procedures can be at least in part attributed to the online culture around beauty standards. This is a distinctly negative development, because it exploits deep-seated insecurities, especially in young people and might lead to decisions that have a detrimental effect on a person's future.
